coverage.notes: Every rule rests on one course (ENGR 315 Lab), its first two weeks, one instructor-supplied m-file template, two lab handouts, and one student's m-files and reports. No other course has MATLAB files: listing both of the student's archives (his iCloud term folders and his university OneDrive) in September 2026 found .m, .mlx and .slx files under ENGR 315 Lab only. Simulink is named in the Lab 1 title but no Simulink evidence exists, so Simulink is not covered at all. Control System Toolbox functions (tf, step, pzmap, rlocus) are not covered: the labs seen so far use closed-form expressions and base MATLAB only. The exemplars have never been run in MATLAB. Where another course uses MATLAB, treat these as a starting point and read that course's handout first. The host cannot execute MATLAB: every number and figure comes from the student's own run, so nothing a script produces is verified until the student returns its printed output and figure.

scope.rule: Observed in ENGR 315 Lab only. The header block and file naming are course-specific; the plotting and script rules are general enough to carry to other courses unless their handout says otherwise.
scope.basis: ENGR 315 Lab 1 and Lab 2 handouts; the instructor m-file template; the student's Week 1 and Week 2 m-files.

trademark.rule: Write MATLAB in capitals in reports and prose, never Matlab or MatLab.

script_not_command_window.rule: Work goes in a script (m-file) that runs top to bottom and regenerates every result. Commands typed at the prompt are not the deliverable; the handout asks for the commands to be run from an m-file even when they could be typed.

header_block.rule: Every m-file opens with the instructor template's comment header: course line, Author, Date with a version number, Title, File Name, then clc, close all, and clear all, each with a short comment. The File Name line must match the saved file name.
header_block.note: The template warns against clear all when a Simulink model reads workspace variables. Keep that caveat when a lab moves to Simulink.
header_block.basis: Instructor m-file template (Week 1); every student m-file in Weeks 1 and 2 keeps it.

file_naming.rule: One m-file per experiment, named [StudentName]_Lab[N]_Ex[M]_v[K].m, copied forward and renamed rather than edited in place when the next experiment builds on it. Where one m-file covers the whole lab, [StudentName]_Lab[N]_v[K].m.
file_naming.note: The written sources disagree on the name part: the Lab 1 handout says the student's name, the template header says first and last name separated by an underscore, and the Lab 2 guidelines say the file name should include the student's initials. The submitted files used surname and given name run together. When a handout names a pattern, the current handout wins.
file_naming.basis: ENGR 315 Lab 1 handout (Experiments 2 and 3); the template header; the Lab 2 guidelines' formatting checklist; the student's submitted file names.

elementwise_operators.rule: Use .* ./ .^ whenever either operand is a vector of time or x samples. Plain * between two vectors of the same shape is a dimension error, not an elementwise product.
elementwise_operators.basis: ENGR 315 Lab 1 handout (Experiment 4 asks what happens without the period); Lab 2 handout (use .* between the exponential and the sine).

exponential.rule: Write exp(x). MATLAB has no built-in constant e, so e^x fails unless e was defined.
exponential.basis: An early Week 2 student draft written with e^ that never ran, replaced in the working file by exp().

loops_over_cases.rule: Put the cases in one vector and fill one row of a preallocated matrix per case inside a for loop. Do not repeat near-identical lines per case.
loops_over_cases.basis: ENGR 315 Lab 2 handout (use a for loop, do not repeat similar code) and its hint skeleton; the student's Week 2 m-file.

one_plot_call.rule: Draw all the cases with a single plot command taking several x, y, style triples, and keep the returned handles.
one_plot_call.basis: ENGR 315 Lab 2 handout; the student's Week 2 m-file.

grayscale_line_styles.rule: Each curve on a shared figure gets its own line style (solid, dashed, dash-dot, dotted), not only its own color, so the plot reads on a black-and-white printout. Four styles exist; a fifth trace needs markers or a gray shade to stay distinct.
grayscale_line_styles.basis: ENGR 315 Lab 2 handout and formatting checklist (plots must look different in black and white).

labels_title_legend.rule: ENGR 315: every figure has a title inside the plot, both axes labeled with the quantity and unit, and a legend naming every trace the reader must tell apart. The in-plot title is a course-specific requirement: other courses' report standards (ENGR 204 Lab, for one) say a captioned figure carries no title inside the graph. Follow the course, not this pack's default.
labels_title_legend.basis: ENGR 315 Lab 2 handout (asks for a title, axis labels and a legend, with an example title); Lab 1 template script; the ENGR 204 Lab pack's plot rules for the contrast.

greek_in_text.rule: Greek letters and subscripts use TeX markup in titles, labels, and legends: \zeta, \omega_n, \tau. A legend that spells out 'zeta' is wrong.
greek_in_text.basis: ENGR 315 Lab 2 handout; Lab 1 template script (\omega_n in the label).

no_figure_touch_up.rule: The figure the script produces is the figure in the report. Limits, labels, styles, and legend are all set in code, never with the figure window's editing tools.

overlays.rule: Add curves to an existing axes with hold on, and close with hold off. Pass the legend only the handles it should name.
overlays.basis: ENGR 315 Lab 2 handout (Experiment 2 uses hold on); the student's Week 2 m-file (legend built from selected handles).

code_in_report.rule: The m-files are part of the deliverable: included in the report (in the body or an appendix that the body refers to) and also uploaded as .m files.
code_in_report.basis: ENGR 315 Lab 1 handout (m-files included and uploaded, with a penalty when they are not uploaded); Lab 2 checklist.

individual_files.rule: Each student writes and runs their own m-files. Discussing is allowed; running a classmate's file to get results is treated as plagiarism.

methods.title: Plot a closed-form response across a parameter sweep
methods.when: A handout gives an analytical response y(t) and asks for several values of one parameter on one figure.
steps: Start from the course header template and fill in every header field.
Define the time vector with a step small enough to show the fastest feature, and a span long enough for the slowest case to settle.
Put the parameter values in one vector; the handout usually fixes which regimes must appear.
Preallocate the output matrix with zeros(number of cases, length(t)).
Fill one row per case in a for loop, using elementwise operators on t.
Before plotting, print a check value per case that has a known answer (the initial condition, or a value at a characteristic time).
Plot all rows with one plot call, one black line style per case, then title, labels with units, and a TeX legend.
Set axis limits in code so the interesting part of the response fills the plot.
pitfalls: A formula that divides by a quantity that is zero at a boundary value (for example sqrt(1 - zeta^2) at zeta = 1). Use a value just inside the boundary, as the handout specifies, and say why in the report.

Past that boundary the square root turns imaginary and acos returns a complex angle. MATLAB then plots only the real part with a warning, and a branch sign can flip the whole curve. Wrap the whole expression, not part of it, and check the printed initial value equals the given initial condition for every case.
A time step too coarse for the fastest case, which draws a smooth-looking but wrong curve.
methods.basis: ENGR 315 Lab 2 handout and hint skeleton; the student's Week 2 m-file and its separate output-check notes, which name a sign flip in the overdamped case as the failure to look for.

methods.title: Polynomial roots from a coefficient vector
methods.when: Characteristic equations, pole locations, or a handout that says to use roots.
steps: Write the coefficients in descending powers, with an explicit 0 for every missing power.
Call roots on the vector and report complex pairs as a +/- b j.
Cross-check a quadratic factor with the quadratic formula when the handout asks for hand work too.
pitfalls: Dropping the zero for a missing power, which silently solves a different polynomial.
methods.basis: ENGR 315 Lab 1 handout (Experiment 6); the student's Week 1 m-file.

methods.title: Independent expected values before the screenshot
methods.when: Any figure that goes into a report.
steps: Compute a few expected values independently of the plot: initial value, final value, a characteristic time, a ratio with a closed form.
Have the script print the same quantities and compare.
Only then export or screenshot the figure.
pitfalls: Reading values off the plot and calling that a check.
Fixing a curve that looks wrong but is physically right; know which behavior the analysis expects before editing.
methods.basis: The student's Week 2 output-check notes, which listed expected values and visual checks before the figure was captured.

methods.title: Hand the script over and ask for the right things back
methods.when: Always. The host has no MATLAB, and no exemplar here has been run.
steps: Give the student the complete m-file, header filled with placeholders they replace.
Tell them to save it under the File Name in its header, then run the whole file (Run or F5), not pasted lines.
Ask for the printed check values, any warning or error text verbatim, and the exported figure.
pitfalls: Treating an unrun script as verified.
A warning about ignored imaginary parts is a result that needs fixing, not noise.
methods.basis: Tool constraint; the output-check practice in the Week 2 student notes.

exemplars.shows: Course template header with placeholder identity, File Name matching the saved name, clc / close all / clear all with the Simulink caveat.
Invented first-order RC sweep over tau: preallocated matrix, for loop, elementwise operators, printed self-check, one plot call in black line styles, TeX legend.
Invented step response with reference lines added by hold on / hold off, a gray shade for a fourth style, legend built from selected handles.
